role.altitude: The ophthalmologist keeps examining, interpreting, deciding, educating and talking with patients; retyping medication, lens data and measurements, searching device viewers and typing notes shrink.
skills_to_grow: Correcting scribe drafts and using a central image archive
role.ambitious_version: An ophthalmologist who sees every earlier test at a glance.

tasks.short: Review history, results and images, discuss options, risks, benefits and goals with the patient, decide and write the treatment plan, fill the surgery booking, give consent forms and leaflets, discuss complex cases with the team and answer patient questions to develop treatment plans.

steps.what: Ophthalmologist reviews the history, test results and images
Ophthalmologist discusses options, treatment risks and benefits and the patient's goals
Ophthalmologist decides the treatment plan
Ophthalmologist writes the treatment plan in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft of the treatment plan in the record template.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consultation transcript, and every item in the transcript missing from the draft; the ophthalmologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed item and corrects every line before it is saved. A monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The ophthalmologist writes it when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Ophthalmologist fills the surgery booking form: retyping patient details, procedure and lens data today; filled from the plan and biometry after the change
Ophthalmologist checks the final booking: patient, eye, procedure and lens power against the plan and biometry
Ophthalmologist releases the checked booking to surgery planning
Ophthalmologist chooses the consent form and procedure leaflet: printed today, picked for the portal after the change
Ophthalmologist checks the consent form and leaflet match the planned procedure and eye, and that they go to this patient
Ophthalmologist sends the checked consent form and leaflet to the patient portal
Ophthalmologist discusses complex cases in the team meeting
Ophthalmologist answers patient questions in the portal

tasks.design: With consent, a certified scribe drafts the treatment plan, and the ophthalmologist corrects it. The surgery booking fills patient details, procedure and lens data from the plan and biometry, instead of retyping; the ophthalmologist checks it and releases it once. The ophthalmologist checks the consent form and leaflet and sends them once to the patient portal. Reviewing, discussing, deciding, the team meeting and questions stay with the ophthalmologist.

approvals.approved_version: The surgery booking with patient, eye, procedure and lens power exactly as checked by the ophthalmologist in s5c, released once to surgery planning; any change needs a new check.
The consent form and leaflet for this procedure and eye exactly as checked by the ophthalmologist in s6c, sent once to this patient's portal; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were typed and bookings filled by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Certified scribes and booking forms filled from the record.
tasks.still_hard: Patients weighing risky surgery for small gains.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a patient choose between seeing better and risking worse.

reach.learn: Whether they get the leaflet before deciding.

evidence.claim: In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
A clinical scribe and coding tool carries MDR class IIa.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.
Health data are special category data; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: developing treatment plans; collaborating with multidisciplinary teams (task 17165) and consulting with other professionals (task 17159) are sibling tasks.
s7 is discussion in the team meeting; it is conversation and keeps its full time.

Each task in this set carries the scribe or template saving only for its own part of the record: the history in task 17167, the treatment plan in task 17171, the education note in task 17163 and the test interpretation in task 17170.
s4 is priced at 75; s5 saves retyping data already in the record and keeps 30; s6 keeps half for choosing the forms; the booking and form checks and releases keep their full time.
The means prior puts 25% on documents; the steps show 31%, because reviewing results and writing the plan take more desk time.
unknowns: Share of patients who consent to recording.
research_questions: Do surgery bookings carry fewer lens data errors?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients agree to recording (s4 keeps 92) and lens data often need retyping (s5 keeps 70) (1.6); high: surgery-heavy clinics with most patients recorded (4.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Educate patients about maintenance and promotion of healthy vision, demonstrate eye drops and lid hygiene, give leaflets, note the education, answer follow-up questions and set screening recalls.

steps.what: Ophthalmologist educates patients about maintenance and promotion of healthy vision
Ophthalmologist demonstrates eye drop technique and lid hygiene
Ophthalmologist selects leaflets: printed today, picked from vetted texts for the portal after the change
Ophthalmologist checks the leaflets fit this patient's condition and the advice given, and that they go to this patient
Ophthalmologist sends the checked leaflets to the patient portal
Ophthalmologist notes the education in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft of the education note in the record template.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consultation transcript, and every item in the transcript missing from the draft; the ophthalmologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed item and corrects every line before it is saved. A monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The ophthalmologist writes it when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

steps.what: Ophthalmologist writes replies to follow-up questions: from scratch today, from drafts citing vetted texts after the change

loop.input: The patient's question and vetted, guideline-based patient texts.
loop.output: A draft reply citing the text it draws on.
loop.check: Each reply sentence must cite its vetted paragraph. A second check reads each sentence against the cited paragraph and flags sentences the paragraph does not support; questions about new symptoms get no draft and the ophthalmologist answers them by hand.
loop.stop: Questions about the patient's own diagnosis go to the ophthalmologist unanswered.
loop.why_not_simpler: Patients ask in their own words.

steps.what: Ophthalmologist checks the final reply: advice against the question, the record and the vetted texts, and that it goes to this patient
Ophthalmologist sends the checked reply in the portal
Ophthalmologist sets diabetic and glaucoma screening recalls by hand

tasks.design: Leaflets from vetted, guideline-based texts are chosen, checked and sent once to the patient portal. With consent, the scribe drafts the education note. Follow-up replies start from drafts citing vetted texts; the ophthalmologist adapts each, checks the final reply and sends it once. Screening recalls are set from the diagnosis code, and the ophthalmologist confirms them. Educating and demonstrating stay with the ophthalmologist.

approvals.approved_version: The leaflets exactly as checked by the ophthalmologist in s3c, sent once to this patient's portal; any change needs a new check.
Each reply exactly as checked by the ophthalmologist in s5c, sent once in the portal to the patient who asked; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Leaflets were printed and recalls set by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Portal leaflets, scribes, reply drafting with citations and coded recalls.
tasks.human_edge: Persuading a diabetic patient that screening protects their sight.

evidence.claim: A patient information site is guideline-based and written with professional bodies and a patients' federation.
In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: educating patients on healthy vision; diagnosing and treating eye disorders (task 17176) is a sibling task.

Each task in this set carries the scribe or template saving only for its own part of the record: the history in task 17167, the treatment plan in task 17171, the education note in task 17163 and the test interpretation in task 17170.
s3 keeps half; s4 is priced at 75; s5 keeps 70 because each draft is adapted; s6 keeps 30 for confirming recalls; the leaflet and reply checks and sends keep their full time.
The means prior puts 15% on documents; the steps show 9%, because education happens in the room.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few patients use the portal (s3 keeps 80), few agree to recording (s4 keeps 95) and few questions fit a draft (s5 keeps 95) (4.3); high: large diabetic and glaucoma lists using the portal (7.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Let patients fill a pre-visit questionnaire, review referrals and records, take the history, retype medication and allergies, copy questionnaire answers, request outside records, evaluate risk factors and document patients' medical histories.

steps.what: Patient fills the pre-visit eye and medical history questionnaire in the portal
Ophthalmologist reviews the referral letter and earlier records
Ophthalmologist takes the history in conversation with the patient
Ophthalmologist retypes medication and allergies from the referral letter
Ophthalmologist copies questionnaire answers into the record
Ophthalmologist requests records from other hospitals by mail and phone
Ophthalmologist evaluates patients' medical histories for risk factors such as diabetes and anticoagulants
Ophthalmologist documents the history in the record

loop.input: The recorded consultation, with the patient's consent, and the structured data in the record.
loop.output: A draft of the history in the record template.
loop.check: A check lists every statement in the draft that cannot be found in the consultation transcript or the questionnaire, and every item in the transcript missing from the draft; the ophthalmologist reads the draft against the consult, resolves each listed item and corrects every line before it is saved. A monthly sample audit looks for omissions.
loop.stop: The ophthalmologist writes it when the recording is incomplete or the patient declines recording.

tasks.design: Medication and allergies arrive by integration from the patient's medication overview, instead of retyping them. Questionnaire answers flow into the record. With consent, the scribe drafts the history, and the ophthalmologist corrects it before it is saved. Reviewing, the conversation, requesting records and evaluating risks stay with the ophthalmologist.
tasks.previous_blocker: Medication, answers and histories were typed by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Medication integration, portal questionnaires and certified scribes.
tasks.human_edge: Asking the question that reveals a hidden risk.

evidence.claim: In a peer-reviewed study of 236,153 scribe notes, self-estimated time per note fell from 6.69 to 4.72 minutes; three of seven authors were from the vendor.
A clinical scribe and coding tool carries MDR class IIa.
Ambient recording captures staff performance and needs works council consent.
Health data are special category data; expect a DPIA.

assumptions: Boundary: documenting and evaluating histories; diagnosing and treating eye disorders (task 17176) is a sibling task.

Each task in this set carries the scribe or template saving only for its own part of the record: the history in task 17167, the treatment plan in task 17171, the education note in task 17163 and the test interpretation in task 17170.
Input contract for s4: about 60% of patients have a medication overview available by integration; s4 is priced at that share and keeps 40.
s5 saves copying answers the patient already entered and keeps 20; s8 is priced at 70.
The means prior puts 58% in person; the steps show 40%, because reading referrals and writing the history take about 40%.
Patients' questionnaire time is shown in s1.
unknowns: Share of patients completing the questionnaire.
research_questions: Do medication errors in the record fall?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: only a third of patients have an overview by integration (s4 keeps 70), half fill the questionnaire (s5 keeps 60) and few agree to recording (s8 keeps 90) (6.2); high: coverage as assumed (15.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order tests, perform slit lamp examination, gonioscopy and tonometry, interpret OCT scans, visual fields and photographs, find earlier tests in device viewers, copy device measurements, write the interpretation, discuss results with patients and colleagues and answer messages to perform, order or interpret diagnostic tests.

steps.what: Ophthalmologist orders diagnostic tests such as OCT, visual fields and angiography
Ophthalmologist performs slit lamp examination, gonioscopy and tonometry
Ophthalmologist interprets the results of OCT scans, visual fields and photographs
Ophthalmologist finds earlier tests in separate device viewers to compare
Ophthalmologist copies device measurements such as eye pressure, axial length and keratometry into the record
Ophthalmologist writes the test interpretation
Ophthalmologist discusses results with the patient
Ophthalmologist answers patient messages about results
Ophthalmologist discusses unclear images with colleagues

tasks.design: Imaging devices send their results to one image archive that shows earlier tests side by side, instead of opening each device viewer. Device measurements import into the record. The interpretation template opens with the measurements filled, and the ophthalmologist writes the findings and conclusion. Ordering, examining, interpreting, discussing results and messages stay with the ophthalmologist. No model reads the images.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier tests were scattered across device viewers and measurements typed.
tasks.enabler_now: Central image archives and device integration with the record.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing progression that no single measurement shows.
tasks.altitude: Less searching and typing; interpretation stays.

reach.learn: Whether change over time is shown clearly.

evidence.claim: Device measurements imported into the record replace typing.
Decision software is usually MDR class IIa or higher.
The dossier is kept twenty years after the last change.

assumptions: Boundary: performing, ordering and interpreting tests; diagnosing and treating eye disorders (task 17176) is a sibling task.

Each task in this set carries the scribe or template saving only for its own part of the record: the history in task 17167, the treatment plan in task 17171, the education note in task 17163 and the test interpretation in task 17170.
s4 keeps 40 for older devices; s5 saves typing values already in the device and keeps 20; s6 keeps 75 because findings are written by hand.
The means prior puts 7% on screens; the steps show 35%, because scans, fields and photographs are read on screens.

incremental.description: No new work: devices send results to the archive and the record without the ophthalmologist; the imaging team keeps the links.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many older devices are not linked, so viewers are opened and values typed for them (s4 keeps 70, s5 keeps 60) (6.3); high: devices linked as designed (10.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
